quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The first vowel is long and open, and the ch is /k/.
quests.explanation: The ch is /k/ and the stress lands on the first syllable, where the vowel is long and open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If you can hold the vowel indefinitely with an open mouth, it is /ɑː/. /æ/ is quick and bright.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Wide jaw at the start, with weak syllables after it.
quests.explanation: The wide vowel is in the stressed first syllable, and the later vowels are weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so the only question is how high the front of the tongue rises.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ea is short in this word.
quests.explanation: Ea spells the half-open vowel here, as in 'zealous' and 'head'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ has the jaw half open and the tongue mid-front; /æ/ needs the jaw dropped clearly lower, tongue low and forward, mouth wide.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: A short central vowel comes before the stressed glide.
quests.explanation: The first syllable has the short central vowel. The stressed second syllable has a glide that isn't part of this choice.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If /ʌ/ keeps coming out as /ɒ/, relax the lips completely and let the tongue rest in the middle.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The con- is stressed and short in this word.
quests.explanation: The sc spells /ʃ/ in this word, and the con- is short and rounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is back and open with slightly rounded lips; /ʌ/ is central and unrounded with neutral lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The au spelling, then /ʃ/.
quests.explanation: The au spelling is dependable for the long rounded vowel, and the -tious ending is weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Don't add an r in RP, but remember the vowel carries the whole syllable, so hold /ɔː/ fully.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The stressed syllable begins with a three-consonant cluster.
quests.explanation: The stressed second syllable has the long vowel and the initial syllable is weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Try whispering: even without voice the difference in tongue height is audible, which shows that quality, not just length, carries the contrast.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Listen for the gliding vowel after /sw/.
quests.explanation: The ua spells /weɪ/ here, and the glide sits in the stressed second syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Time the vowel: /e/ is over quickly, while /eɪ/ carries on and ends with the tongue rising.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: After the weak first syllable, keep the er steady and unrounded.
quests.explanation: Er is normally the steady central vowel in stressed syllables, and the s sounds like /z/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ is central with neutral or slightly spread lips; /ɔː/ is back with clearly rounded lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: After the weak first syllable, listen for a wide-open start.
quests.explanation: The wide-start diphthong is in the stressed second syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling traps: ow can be /aʊ/ (cow) or /əʊ/ (slow), and ou is /aʊ/ in out but /əʊ/ in soul.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The oa spelling: the lips close up in the stressed syllable.
quests.explanation: The oa spelling closes the lips in a glide in the stressed second syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: o_e and oa mostly spell /əʊ/, while a single o in a short closed syllable (hot, shop) is usually /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FINAL SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The main stress falls on the final syllable, after an unstressed -in-.
quests.explanation: The final syllable has the open-start diphthong. The first syllable has a different diphthong with secondary stress.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both end in a glide towards /ɪ/, but /aɪ/ starts wide open and /eɪ/ starts mid-front.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Hold a long rounded vowel on the stressed syllable and don't shorten it as in 'forest'.
quests.explanation: The or isn't short here, unlike in 'forest'. It takes the long rounded vowel in the stressed syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Words spelled aw or au (saw, sauce) take /ɔː/ reliably, while a after w can go either way.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ar signals a long open vowel.
quests.explanation: Ar signals the long open vowel in the stressed first syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: BATH words (class, path, plant, dance, half) are one of the biggest differences between RP and other accents. Follow the RP set.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ch is /k/ again. The jaw is half open.
quests.explanation: The ch is /k/ again, and the half-open vowel is in the stressed first syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Check the mouth opening: roughly one finger-width for /e/, closer to two stacked fingers for /æ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FINAL SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Four syllables; the glide is in the last.
quests.explanation: The glide is in the final stressed syllable. The earlier syllables are weak or secondary and have no glide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The cue is movement: /ɪə/ travels towards the centre, while /iː/ stays high and front throughout.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FINAL SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The last syllable carries the stress and is held.
quests.explanation: The final stressed syllable has the long vowel. The earlier short vowels are not the target.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A voiceless consonant after the vowel shortens both. If duration seems to vanish, rely on the tense quality of /iː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The silent h makes the o the start of the second syllable.
quests.explanation: The silent h makes the o the start of the stressed second syllable, which is short and rounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Round the lips a little and drop the jaw for /ɒ/. Keep them flat and relaxed for /ʌ/, with the tongue further forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The first syllable is stressed and long, and the lips round.
quests.explanation: The first syllable is stressed and long, unlike the short u in 'put'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Push the lips into a small circle for /uː/. For /ʊ/ the rounding is slack and the tongue sits lower and further forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FINAL SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The last syllable is stressed and starts with rounded lips.
quests.explanation: The final syllable has a rounded-start glide. The first syllable has the central vowel, which isn't part of this choice.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both glide to /ɪ/, so listen to the first half: rounded and darker for /ɔɪ/, open and brighter for /aɪ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Listen for an open start on -cy-, the stressed syllable.
quests.explanation: The stressed second syllable has the open-start diphthong. The re- has secondary stress and a long vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The jaw starts lower for /aɪ/ and visibly closes. /eɪ/ starts nearly half closed and moves less.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Strong first syllable with a wide jaw; the /tʃ/ opens it.
quests.explanation: A wide vowel in the stressed first syllable, with a weak second syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is longer and more spread than /e/. Learners often use /e/ for both, so exaggerate the jaw drop at first.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: After the weak first syllable, the stressed vowel is pushed out and held.
quests.explanation: The weak first syllable is schwa, and the stressed second syllable has the long rounded vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are rounded, so rounding alone will not separate them: /uː/ is purer and longer, /ʊ/ brief and a little more open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: No lip rounding; the ur is steady.
quests.explanation: The u spelling here is the steady vowel, not the 'cut' type.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling will not decide: ir, er, ur, ear and wor- give /ɜː/, while u, o and ou usually give /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FINAL SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Listen at the very end of the word: the final syllable is the strong one.
quests.explanation: The first syllable has a closing glide with secondary stress. The final syllable carries the main stress.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is lower and more central than /iː/ on the chart, so the tongue shifts slightly down and back.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The or before th: long and rounded.
quests.explanation: The or before th is long and rounded, and the th is voiced.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If your /ɒ/ comes out too long, shorten it and open the jaw rather than rounding tighter.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Half-open jaw in the first syllable.
quests.explanation: The first syllable has the half-open vowel. The final -ate keeps a glide, but it isn't part of this pair.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Tongue height is the cue: it falls from mid-front /e/ to low-front /æ/. Lips are slightly spread for both.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The stressed second syllable is short, with a small mouth gap.
quests.explanation: The stressed second syllable is short, and the first syllable is also a weak KIT-like vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is lax and slightly lowered; /iː/ is higher and tenser with spread lips. Quality carries the contrast, and length only reinforces it.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The y spells a short vowel.
quests.explanation: The y spells the short vowel in the first syllable, as in 'gym'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Duration is similar, so rely on openness: a small mouth gap for /ɪ/, a slightly larger one for /e/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A gliding vowel, then /tf/.
quests.explanation: A gliding vowel in the stressed first syllable, and the -ful ending is weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The end of /eɪ/ is a tiny /ɪ/. If the word finishes with a faint 'ee', it is /eɪ/.
